benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Jumped to about $109.86 on 17 Oct (Trading Economics), up roughly 3.7% on the day, after UKMTO said most Hormuz-area tanker attacks go unreported and counted far fewer AIS-tracked transits than the US claims, and the IEA moved to accelerate emergency releases. Week-ago is the 16 Oct value from this site's own prior run.

benchmarks.label: Henry Hub
benchmarks.note: Eased to about $3.12 on 17 Oct (Trading Economics); pre-crisis is the EIA spot price on 27 Feb (FRED). US LNG feedgas and exports are near records, but the US price stays largely insulated from the Hormuz and Red Sea turmoil.

note: Brent and WTI jumped after UKMTO said most Hormuz-area tanker attacks go unreported, with only 42 AIS-tracked transits in a week against the US's claimed 400, and the IEA moved to speed up roughly 100 million barrels of emergency releases including over 20 million of diesel. TTF held near its fresh 2026 high and Henry Hub eased slightly. VLCC freight rates eased about 8% week on week from record highs as Middle East demand cooled and Washington weighed easing shadow-fleet tanker sanctions.
